text:
maria: heads-up, after the hotswap work we still observed a UAF in staging when a tenant kvcache entry was moved between pools. who owns the final visibility guarantee when a runtime holds a pointer during migration?

josh: yeah saw that. my assumption was allocator exposes a reservation token and migration does token->handoff->release. but we never specified how long the runtime's pipeline can safely deref the pointer.

anika: the repro shows allocator demote->free racing with decode. runtime had an outstanding pointer into a slab that allocator freed. crash on decode.

maria: short logs (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-22T18:42:12Z] runtime: kvcache lock range 0x7ff..0x8ff
[2026-03-22T18:42:12Z] allocator: demote range 0x7ff..0x8ff -> staging
[2026-03-22T18:42:12Z] runtime: spawn async decode using pointer (observed)
[2026-03-22T18:42:12Z] allocator: free staging range after demote
[2026-03-22T18:42:12Z] runtime: decode reads freed memory -> crash
```

taylor: ugly. Two families of fixes: runtime-side stronger holds (pin/RC) or allocator-side conservative delays (epochs/grace). both have perf costs.

anika: proposal: explicit observe()/unobserve() API on ranges. allocator keeps per-range observer count; free is deferred while count>0. sample API:
```
Allocator::observe(range) -> ObservationToken
drop(ObservationToken) -> allocator.decrement_observers(range)
Allocator::free(range) checks observers==0
```
This pushes pins to runtime callers that know when they finish.

devon: minimal allocator churn is nice. main worry: token leaks (stuck counts) leading to allocation stalls. need leak detectors/timeouts.

josh: other option: epoch-based grace where runtime records current epoch when it grabs a pointer; free waits until epoch advances. less explicit in runtime but adds allocator bookkeeping and can increase reuse latency.

maria: tradeoffs: explicit tokens = precise, low background work, requires runtime change and leak safeguards; epochs = simpler caller integration, bounded memory but can delay reuse and spike tail latency.

anika: hybrid idea: default "borrow" semantics that are cheap and short-lived for fast paths; long-running async operations request an explicit pin. so most races resolved by cheap borrows, only a few ops pay pin cost.

taylor: important: hotswap transfer semantics. when we move a range between pools, observe tokens must transfer or the transfer must block until observers fall to zero. transfer-blocking hurts availability.

devon: staged handoff pattern: source allocator marks range TRANSFERRING, new allocator installs a proxy mapping to the same physical page. runtime continues to observe original token. transfer completion requires observers==0 on source; then source releases backing and new allocator fully claims mapping. proxies keep correctness but add double-ref bookkeeping.

josh: that's similar to existing pinned-page flow but formalized. downside: metadata bloat and more complex accounting across allocators.

maria: implementation checklist for tokens+proxy approach:
- runtime: observe/unobserve additions to kvcache, decode, prefetch paths
- allocator: per-range observer counter, TRANSFERRING state, proxy entries for incoming transfers
- diagnostics: debug CLI to list ranges by state and observer count; leak detector that alerts/panics after TTL
- emergency fallback: if observer hold-time exceeds threshold, force-copy the page into target pool (expensive but safe)
- tests: unit tests that simulate leaked tokens, ensure fallback copy triggers and no corruption

anika: metrics/alerting: histogram observer hold-times, count of TRANSFERRING ranges, forced-copy rate. create an SLO for forced-copy rate to detect regressions.

taylor: add a debug assert in dev builds to block free if observers>0 so we catch races early. in prod we defer free but instrument heavy.

devon: we should also prototype opt-out epoch mode for very latency-sensitive workloads so users can choose bounded wait vs explicit pins. document the tradeoffs.

josh: product will likely prefer tokens if tail-latency is improved. epochs add N ms reuse windows which can spike tails during bursts.

anika: i'll draft a small RFC with API sketches, a unit test matrix, and a microbenchmark plan. benchmarks: microbatch decode workload with prefetch under three modes: no-observe, borrow-default, explicit-pin. measure tail p99/p999 and memory reuse latency.

maria: who's owning RFC? @anika? please tag eng-sre for alerting knobs and telemetry.

anika: taking it. i'll land a short doc and link back. cc @taylor @devon @josh

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: hotswap-safety-canary on canary1 at 2026-03-23T02:00:00Z :rocket:

taylor: we'll watch canary. if forced-copy rate or long-held observers spike, hold the rollout.

devon: also plan for a canary-era forced-copy budget and an automatic revert if forced-copy > X/min. unit tests need leak simulation.

maria: consensus: proceed with tokens+transfer-proxy for initial rollout, add heavy instrumentation and forced-copy fallback. anika to RFC and bench. thanks all :thumbsup:
